title: A --ready absence assertion passes vacuously if the ready list is empty (the false-pass shape, found in our own suite)
description:
Found by turning opum-cli-e2e TASK-68 finding on this repository own test suite, which is the reciprocal of what they did: having established that "is the value I passed absent?" false-passes for callers of quest (QCLI-297), they asked whether their harness wrote its own absence assertions that way and found three. This is the same question asked of quest-cli tests.

THE DEFECT. test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:936-941 asserts that an archived dependency leaves its dependent excluded from task list --ready:

  expect((json(readyAfterDependencyArchive).data as {id: string}[]).map(t => t.id))
    .not.toContain(dependentId);

Nothing in that row establishes the ready list is non-empty. If --ready returned [] for any unrelated reason the row passes while proving nothing. Its own comment states the intent precisely -- "the fix must not throw, but it must not silently treat an unresolved-then-fixed edge as satisfied either" -- and the assertion covers the first half only. An empty list satisfies it.

The list is probably non-empty in practice, because childId was asserted ready roughly forty lines earlier. That is the actual problem rather than a mitigation: the row validity depends on an unstated invariant established against a DIFFERENT list earlier in the same test. Nothing local to the assertion would fail if that stopped being true.

THE REPAIR IS ONE LINE: assert a known-ready id IS in readyAfterDependencyArchive before asserting dependentId is not, exactly as the sibling row at :893-898 already does (expect(readyIds).toContain(childId) immediately before expect(readyIds).not.toContain(parentId)). The paired form is already the house style twenty lines away -- this row simply does not use it.

SCOPE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED. 83 absence-shaped assertions across test/ (not.toContain, not.toMatch, toBeUndefined, toBeNull, toHaveLength(0), toEqual([])). I inspected the candidates where absence is the CLAIM -- removal, migration, exclusion -- and every other one is paired:
- local-agent-instructions.test.ts:173/183/189/211-212 build their input from BACKLOG_GUIDELINES_BLOCK in the test itself, so presence beforehand is established by construction, and each pairs the absence with a positive assertion.
- fault/git/local-git.test.ts:71 pairs with expect(indexPaths).toContain("unrelated.txt").
- cli-semantics.test.ts:898 pairs with expect(readyIds).toContain(childId).
So this is one row, not a pattern. Recording the negative result too, because "I checked and found one" and "I found one" are different claims and only the first says anything about the rest.

THIS REPOSITORY HAS NO EQUIVALENT OF THEIR STRUCTURAL BYPASS. Their check.custom takes an already-computed boolean, so all 479 call sites compute the predicate outside the layer their mutation self-test proves -- the self-test is structurally incapable of seeing the class. Nothing analogous here: these are plain expect() calls with no intermediate proven layer to bypass. Different repositories, same defect class, different reason nothing caught it.

QUEUED POST-PUBLISH DELIBERATELY. test/ is not in the published package files list, but a source-touching change re-fires source-gates and alters the tree that has been qualified for 0.7.0. A test hardening that is not urgent does not justify touching a frozen tree, which is the same discipline being applied to QCLI-297.

CORRECTIONS TO THE TEXT ABOVE, marked here rather than silently repaired so the original filing stays readable and the stale sentence stops being quotable. Two claims in this description are withdrawn as of 2026-09-15; the DEFECT and THE REPAIR are unaffected:
  - "The paired form is already the house style twenty lines away." The distance is 38 lines, measured in the file, across a context switch into a fresh setup block -- the 20 was an external figure about this repository repeated without opening the file. And "house style" is itself withdrawn: on all three instances cited as evidence of it, the positive assertion is explained by the test's own subject rather than by a pairing practice, so the SCOPE paragraph's ratio counted co-occurrence and reported compliance.
  - The SCOPE paragraph presents 83 as a population. It is the count from six patterns chosen without justification, of which 21 were actually read. See the implementation notes for the full query, what it omitted, and why the one-row conclusion survives all of it anyway.

acceptanceCriteria.text: test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:936-940 asserts a known-ready id IS present in readyAfterDependencyArchive before asserting dependentId is absent, so an empty ready list fails the row instead of passing it

The repair is verified by making it fail on purpose: with the presence assertion in place, a deliberately emptied ready list must turn the row red -- a hardening that is not shown to fail is not shown to assert anything. The property being restored is SELF-SUFFICIENCY, not correctness: a row that is correct but still depends on an invariant 38 lines away has had the symptom fixed, not the defect

The negative result is preserved WITH ITS QUERY: the record states the exact pattern set searched, justifies why that set defines absence-shaped assertions, and confirms the inspection was exhaustive over it rather than over a convenient subset -- or says how many were read versus counted. A count without its query cannot be read: the first pass reported 83 from six patterns without justifying the set, 55 further assertions matched patterns it had omitted, and only 21 were actually read The CLASSIFICATION RULE is stated alongside the query, because a denominator needs both: a positive counts as pairing only if it establishes the absence check's precondition over the SAME SUBJECT and the SAME SOURCE, and the record names WHICH precondition. Criterion borrowed from opum-cli-e2e AC12, 2026-09-15, verified here by applying it to three rows in this repository rather than adopting it on report -- it reclassifies :895/:898 as paired and leaves :936-940 unpaired for a structural reason. A same-source positive establishing the WRONG precondition does not count: :931 already asserts exitCode toBe(0) over the same invocation, which proves the command succeeded and not that the list is populated.
Ships after the 0.7.0 publish and does not alter the qualified 0.7.0 tree

An EXPLICIT call is recorded on whether a mechanism (lint rule, paired-assertion helper) is warranted, with the reasoning either way -- a recorded no is a complete answer, a silent no is not. It is made only AFTER AC3 produces a denominator that survives its own query being stated, never on hand-found instances. BOTH former arms of this tension are withdrawn as of 2026-09-15: the distance evidence is withdrawn at source (their paired row comes AFTER the unpaired one, in the next scenario, so no author applied the rule and then dropped it) and the 82-of-83 convention evidence counted co-occurrence rather than compliance (on all three instances cited as house style, the positive assertion is explained by the test's own subject). The call is therefore made on ONE known row with no measured base rate on either side, and must SAY that rather than substituting a fresh number for the withdrawn ones

The threshold that would change the mechanism call is named and checkable: a second unpaired row found after the enumeration closes, or any unpaired absence assertion in code written AFTER this task is recorded

Every external measurement this task relies on is marked with its source, its date, and whether this repository verified it independently. As recorded 2026-09-15 and NONE verified here: opum-cli-e2e 479 check.custom call sites, 37 leading-negation candidates, 3 unpaired absence assertions, and 13 lines between their paired and unpaired rows. The in-repo distance is 38 lines, measured here, correcting a 20 this task previously carried on their report without checking a file it owns. WITHDRAWAL, 2026-09-15: the last external figure is withdrawn by its author -- the 13 is correct, the ORDER is reversed -- and the withdrawal was verified here in their file rather than taken on report. AC7's limit, stated so it is known where it stops: it records provenance and cannot detect a withdrawn or misread measurement, and the withdrawn citation here would have carried an accurate marking throughout

Every figure the AC5 call rests on is RE-MEASURED at the moment the call is made -- in the file, by the repository that owns the file -- and a figure carried forward from an earlier report is not admissible input to it. All three errors in this exchange share that one shape and nothing else: their assertion order, the 20-line in-repo distance, and the 83 denominator were each measured once, repeated, and never re-opened at the point they became load-bearing. Note what this does NOT ask for, because the cheaper versions are the ones that already failed: not verify-the-peer, since two of the three were self-inflicted on files the claimant owned, and not a marking, since AC7 marks and would have marked this one correctly

plan: Re-measure the absence-assertion population in test/ with an explicitly stated query and classification rule (AC3/AC8), in the file, by this repository
Repair the unpaired row at test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:941-945 by asserting a known-ready id IS present before asserting dependentId is absent (AC1)
Prove the repair fails on purpose: with the presence assertion in place, empty the ready list and confirm the row goes red (AC2)
Make the explicit mechanism call on the justified denominator, name the threshold that would change it, and record provenance for every external figure (AC5/AC6/AC7)
run bun run check, commit, review via review-assignment, land
implementationNotes:
THE DISTANCE OBSERVATION, from opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-15 -- and it puts a real tension on this task that should be decided explicitly rather than drifted past.

THEIR MEASUREMENT. The paired form was house style 20 lines away from the unpaired row in this repository (cli-semantics.test.ts:893-898 pairs, :936-941 does not). In their harness the same distance is 13 lines (21-quest-records.mjs:306 pairs, :293 does not). Their conclusion, which I think is right: whatever makes an author pair one assertion and not the next is NOT knowledge of the rule. Both authors had the rule and applied it a few lines earlier. So this is an argument for a MECHANISM over a CONVENTION.

THE TENSION, stated because it cuts against something I wrote on this same task. My own recorded finding is that 82 of 83 absence-shaped assertions here are already paired -- one row, not a pattern -- and I insisted on reporting that negative result because it is what makes the single hit informative. A lint rule or a required-pairing helper built for one row in 83 is over-engineering, and building one would contradict the negative result I went out of my way to record.

Both halves are true and they point opposite ways:
- Mechanism-over-convention says a rule that authors demonstrably fail to apply 13-20 lines after applying it is not a rule a reader can be trusted to follow, and the durable fix is a check.
- The 82/83 ratio says the convention is in fact being followed almost everywhere, and the cost of a mechanism is not obviously repaid by one row.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: silently picking either. Repairing the row and closing is the default path and it would resolve the tension by ignoring it; building a lint rule off one data point is the other failure and it would contradict a finding recorded on this task two notes ago.

DECISION POINT FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS THIS, now AC5: after repairing the row, make an EXPLICIT call on whether a mechanism is warranted, and record the reasoning either way. A recorded "no, one row in 83 does not justify a check, and here is what would change that" is a complete answer. A silent no is not, because the next session finds the same tension with no evidence that anyone weighed it.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER, so the call is checkable rather than a judgement: a second unpaired row found later, or an unpaired row in code written AFTER this task is recorded. Either would move the ratio from "one author slipped once" to "the convention does not hold", which is the threshold their argument actually needs and that a single instance does not meet.

ONE THING THEIR MEASUREMENT SHARPENS ABOUT MY OWN ROW. They note their :293 case at least has its subject in scope, where mine is valid by a coincidence nothing local would notice breaking. That asymmetry matters for the repair: the one-line fix makes the row self-sufficient, not merely correct. That is worth more than the line count suggests and is the reason AC2 asks for the repair to be shown failing on purpose.

MY OWN DENOMINATOR IS WEAKER THAN I REPORTED IT, 2026-09-15. Found by turning opum-cli-e2e argument on myself instead of accepting it, and it matters because they REFUSED my concession specifically on the ground that my number was measured and theirs was not. If that asymmetry is smaller than they think, they are about to build doctrine on a comparison that does not hold.

WHAT I CLAIMED: "83 absence-shaped assertions in test/; every candidate where absence is the CLAIM is paired except one." I presented that as an enumeration.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS, on inspection:

1. THE 83 IS MY PATTERN SET COUNT, NOT THE POPULATION. I grepped six patterns -- not.toContain, not.toMatch, toBeUndefined(), toBeNull(), toHaveLength(0), toEqual([]) -- and never justified the set. Patterns I omitted match 55 more assertions: not.toBe( 49, not.toEqual( 2, .length).toBe(0) 2, toBe(undefined) 1, not.toThrow 1. A denominator is only an enumeration if the thing being enumerated is defined independently of the query that found it. Mine was not.

2. I DID NOT INSPECT ALL 83. I read the 21 not.toContain hits and spot-checked a few others, then wrote "every candidate where absence is the claim", which describes a SELECTION as though it were a sweep. That is the same move I have criticised in relays twice this week.

WHAT I FOUND ON ACTUALLY LOOKING, reported because the conclusion surviving is not the same as the method being sound:
- The 55 are overwhelmingly a DIFFERENT class -- inequality, not collection-absence. exitCode not 0, one id not equal to another, output not this exact string. Most are paired by construction, e.g. asserting a non-zero exit immediately after feeding a known-bad input.
- Only two are genuinely collection-absence: e2e/migration/backlog-preserve-source-ids.test.ts:293 (nothingWritten.length toBe 0) and qcli122-third-pass.test.ts:119 (appliedOperationIds.length toBe 0). BOTH ARE PAIRED. The first sits immediately after an assertion enumerating the specific rejections the run produced, so the run is proven to have done something; the second is guarded by expect(a.kind).toBe("locked") and would fail on undefined anyway, since undefined is not 0.

SO THE ONE-ROW CONCLUSION HOLDS. cli-semantics.test.ts:936-941 is still the only unpaired absence assertion found. Nothing about the finding changes.

WHAT DOES CHANGE IS WHAT THE NUMBER IS ENTITLED TO SUPPORT. "1 in 83" reads as a measured rate. It is one unpaired row in a pattern set I chose, inspected in part. That is further from an enumeration and closer to their three-of-unknown than the comparison they drew allows -- not equal to it, because a defined query over the whole tree is still stronger than hand inspection of a candidate subset, but the gap is narrower than either of us said.

CONSEQUENCE FOR AC5, which is the reason this is not merely a confession. AC5 says a mechanism call needs the number first. It now also needs the number to be worth having: an enumeration whose pattern set is unjustified will produce a confident ratio that means less than it looks like. AC3 amended to require the pattern set be stated and justified, and the inspection to be exhaustive over it rather than over the convenient subset.

THE GENERAL RULE, which is the part worth keeping: a negative result is only as strong as the definition of what was searched. I gave the count and not the query, and a count without its query is the same defect as a claim without its qualifier -- the reader cannot tell what it excludes. The repair is to publish the query alongside the number, every time.

CORRECTION: THE DISTANCE IN THIS REPOSITORY IS 38 LINES, NOT 20 -- and I never measured it before repeating it three times.

MEASURED, in the file itself, 2026-09-15:
  test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:895  expect(readyIds).toContain(childId)        <- the paired form
  test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:898  expect(readyIds).not.toContain(parentId)
  test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts:936-940  the UNPAIRED assertion on dependentId

898 to 936 is 38 lines, not 20. Between them sits an entirely new setup block -- :900-:920 creates a dependency task and a dependent task and archives one -- so the unpaired assertion is not a few lines after the paired one, it is in a different section of the same test after a context switch.

HOW IT GOT IN, which is the only part with any value. "20 lines" was opum-cli-e2e figure about MY repository. I repeated it in a task note, in a pull request body, and in a message back to them, without once opening the file -- in the same exchange in which both of us were arguing about publishing the query alongside the number. A figure about my own code, trivially checkable, taken on report because it arrived inside an argument I agreed with.

THE CORRECTION WEAKENS THE ARGUMENT IT WAS SUPPORTING, which is why it matters rather than being pedantry. The distance claim was: whatever makes an author pair one assertion and not the next is not knowledge of the rule, because both authors applied the rule a few lines earlier. At 20 lines with nothing in between that is persuasive. At 38 lines across a context switch into a fresh setup block it is materially weaker -- "the author forgot the pattern after moving on to a new scenario" is a different and duller claim than "the author applied it and then did not, immediately." Their harness figure of 13 lines may well hold; mine does not support it and I should never have offered it as though it did.

I have not verified their 13. It is their file and their measurement, and this note records it as unverified here rather than repeating the mistake in the opposite direction.

EXTERNAL NUMBERS THIS TASK RESTS ON, now marked rather than implied. opum-cli-e2e named a failure mode they have no answer for: a criterion citing an external measurement inherits that measurement defects, and nothing detects a withdrawn citation -- their AC9 was merged and promoted on my 1-in-83 before I withdrew it. The reciprocal exposure is mine, and it was unmarked until now. This task cites, all from their reports and NONE verified here:
  - 479 check.custom call sites in their harness
  - 37 leading-negation candidates among them
  - 3 unpaired absence assertions found by inspection
  - 13 lines between their paired and unpaired rows
Every one is load-bearing for AC5 reasoning and not one was measured on this side. They are recorded as theirs, dated 2026-09-15, so a later withdrawal has something to land on.

CONVENTION ADOPTED, because a marker nobody applies is worse than none: when a record in this repository cites a measurement taken elsewhere, it names the source, the date, and whether this repository verified it independently. QCLI-289 and QCLI-297 already did this by habit -- "verified independently", "verified at source", "not taken from the relay", "re-measured HERE". QCLI-298 did not, and the 20-line error is what that omission bought.

THE DISTANCE ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AT SOURCE, AND BOTH ARMS OF THE AC5 TENSION ARE NOW GONE. 2026-09-15.

WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, VERIFIED HERE RATHER THAN TAKEN ON REPORT. opum-cli-e2e withdrew the distance argument they contributed to this task. I read their file instead of accepting the withdrawal on their word, because accepting a correction unverified is the same defect as accepting the original claim unverified, just pointing the other way. Measured in /Volumes/external/repos/opum-cli-e2e/suites/21-quest-records.mjs:
  :293       check.custom("promoted draft is gone", ...)  -- UNPAIRED, and FIRST
  :296-300   setup for a different scenario: create a second draft, archive it, two list calls
  :306-307   check.custom("hidden by default") + check.custom("revealed by --include-archived") -- the paired form, and SECOND
The 13 is correct arithmetic on 293 to 306. The ORDER is what the argument needed, and it runs backwards. The claim was that an author applied the rule and then failed to apply it thirteen lines later, so knowledge of the rule cannot be the missing ingredient. What the file shows is an unpaired assertion in one scenario and a paired one in the next. That supports nothing about authors or mechanisms. WITHDRAWN, not weakened -- and with it, the only argument this task carried for a mechanism over a convention.

THE OTHER ARM DOES NOT SURVIVE EITHER, which nobody has said yet and is this repository's half of the reciprocal. The tension recorded on this task had two arms: their distance (mechanism) and my 82-of-83 (convention). Theirs is gone. Mine was already weakened twice -- the denominator is a pattern set I chose, and I inspected a subset -- but there is a third and worse problem in it, found by reading the three instances this task actually cited as evidence of house style:
  - cli-semantics.test.ts:895, expect(readyIds).toContain(childId). The regression under test is that --ready THREW for the whole workspace before the fix. Asserting childId is ready is the fix being verified. That line is there with or without any pairing convention.
  - opum-cli-e2e 21-quest-records.mjs:306-307. The scenario IS that --include-archived reveals the archived draft. The positive assertion is the subject of the test, not a guard on the negative one.
  - fault/git/local-git.test.ts:71, expect(indexPaths).toContain("unrelated.txt"). This one does double duty: the test is about quest committing only its own file and leaving user work staged, so the positive is both subject and guard. It is the one honest instance of the three.
SCOPE, stated so the observation is readable rather than impressive: three instances -- exactly the ones cited on this task as evidence of the convention -- not a re-sweep of the 82. The claim is NOT "no pairing convention exists here". It is that the evidence offered for one measures something else: an absence assertion tends to sit in a test that also asserts something positive, because tests assert positive things. "82 of 83 comply" counted co-occurrence and reported compliance.

WHAT AC5 IS LEFT WITH, and it is less than it looks like losing. Both arms were evidential and both are withdrawn. What survives is the entire original finding, unchanged: cli-semantics.test.ts:936-940 is one row that passes vacuously, and the repair is one line. What is gone is the ability to make the mechanism call by weighing "authors fail thirteen lines later" against "82 of 83 comply", because neither figure is entitled to that weight. The call is now made on ONE known row with no measured base rate on either side. That is the honest input and AC5 should say so rather than reaching for a replacement number -- the reach is what produced both withdrawn figures.

AC7 WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT THIS, AND SAYING SO IS WHAT MAKES IT USABLE. opum-cli-e2e made the point against their own correction: the citation would have read "opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-15, not independently verified", which is accurate, and the claim was still wrong -- it was their own file and their own misreading. Agreed, and recorded as AC7's stated limit rather than as a fault in it. AC7 records PROVENANCE. It does not detect a measurement that was withdrawn, misread, or never taken. A control whose boundary is written down is one a reader knows when to trust; an unbounded one gets trusted everywhere and therefore nowhere.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, now AC8. Re-measure a load-bearing figure AT THE MOMENT a decision rests on it, in the file, by the repository that owns the file. All three errors in this exchange share exactly that shape and nothing else: their ordering, my 20 lines, my 83 -- each was taken once, carried forward, and never re-opened at the point it became load-bearing. Note what this does NOT ask for, because the cheaper version is the one that fails: not "verify the peer", since two of the three were self-inflicted on files the claimant owned, and not a marking, since AC7 already marks and would have marked this one correctly.

THE CARRIER IS THE FINDING. Their framing, and it is right: a figure that arrives inside an argument both parties already hold is not checked by either. They took a number about their own file from nobody and never looked; I took a number about my own file from them and never looked. Two sessions converging fast reads as a quality signal in this fleet, which is exactly the condition under which neither checks. I have deliberately not added a sixth corollary for it, and neither did they -- "verify the thing, not a claim about the thing" is already the first line of the doctrine this sits under. A rule that says "and mean it this time" is not a rule. AC8 is a re-measurement TRIGGER tied to a moment, which is a different thing from a restatement.

AUTHORSHIP WAS THE WRONG AXIS. Their AC12 supplies the structural criterion, and applying it here inverts half of what I sent them. 2026-09-15.

WHAT THEY ADOPTED AND WHAT IT COSTS ME. opum-cli-e2e turned my "the positive is the test's own subject" observation into a binding classification rule on their audit (their AC12): a positive counts as PAIRING only if it establishes the absence check's precondition over the SAME SUBJECT and the SAME SOURCE, and the record must name WHICH precondition. That is a better object than the observation it came from, because it is checkable per row instead of per intuition -- and it does not need to know what the author was thinking, which is exactly where my version went wrong.

APPLIED HERE, IT MOVES BOTH CITED ROWS, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Measured in the file, 2026-09-15:
  - cli-semantics.test.ts:895/:898 COUNTS AS PAIRING under AC12. readyIds is one array from one invocation; expect(readyIds).toContain(childId) establishes non-emptiness over the same subject and source that expect(readyIds).not.toContain(parentId) then reads. It is pairing whatever the author intended, and I classified it as "not pairing" on the ground that the positive exists for the test's own reasons. Intent is not the criterion. Structure is.
  - Their :306-307 does NOT count as pairing under their own AC12, for the same reason in reverse -- see the note below; different invocations, different subjects.
So of the three instances I cited, one flips to paired and one flips to unpaired. The observation I sent was half inverted by the rule it produced.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. cli-semantics.test.ts:936-940 is still unpaired, and now for a STATED structural reason rather than "nothing local would fail": the nearest positive (readyIds at :895) is a different invocation from readyAfterDependencyArchive, so it cannot establish this list's precondition.

AND THE SHARPEST THING THE CRITERION FOUND, which is an argument FOR its second clause. :931 already asserts expect(readyAfterDependencyArchive.exitCode).toBe(0) -- SAME source, SAME subject, and it establishes the WRONG precondition. It proves the command succeeded; the row needs the list to be populated, which a successful command returning [] satisfies while proving nothing. A same-source positive is not sufficient. The load-bearing half of AC12 is "record WHICH precondition", not "same subject and source" -- and this row would pass the first clause and fail the second. Worth stating plainly because the cheaper version of that rule (a positive assertion over the same variable, nearby) is the one anyone would reach for first, and it would have classified this row as safe.

WHAT THIS IS WORTH TO AC3, and it is the reason this note is not merely a correction. AC3 requires a denominator whose QUERY is stated. A denominator also needs its CLASSIFICATION RULE stated, and I had neither: first no query, then a query with "is absence the CLAIM here?" as an unstated judgement call applied by hand. AC12 is that missing second half, and it is borrowed rather than invented. AC3 amended to require both.

DOES THIS REVIVE 82-of-83? No. That ratio was never classified structurally -- it counted co-occurrence by eye, which is the defect, and re-running it under AC12 would be a new measurement with a new number, not a rehabilitation of the old one. AC5 still stands on one known row with no base rate. But the path to a real base rate now exists and is cheap: apply AC12's criterion over AC3's stated query. Whoever makes the AC5 call should do that rather than decide without one -- and under AC8, measure it AT that moment rather than citing this note.

THE OPEN QUESTION THIS LEAVES, AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT ANSWERED HERE. 2026-09-15, closing the opum-cli-e2e exchange.

WHAT THEY FOUND ON THEIR SIDE, reported by them and NOT verified here beyond the one row I did read: their suite has ZERO rows where a positive assertion was written deliberately to guard an absence check. The one survivor they cite (32-lore-workspace.mjs:104) establishes the preceding row's precondition as a SIDE EFFECT of stopping its own every() from passing vacuously. Their AC3 had claimed the repair pattern existed twice; it exists once, incidentally.

THE RECIPROCAL QUESTION FOR THIS REPOSITORY, which is the thing worth carrying forward: is any pairing here deliberate either? On the rows I have actually read -- three, hand-picked, which is why this is a question and not a finding:
  - cli-semantics.test.ts:895 -- structurally paired under AC12, but the positive is the regression under test. Incidental.
  - fault/git/local-git.test.ts:71 -- structurally paired, but the positive asserts user work stayed staged, which is the test's subject. Incidental.
  - cli-semantics.test.ts:931 -- same source, same subject, wrong precondition. Not a guard at all.
Zero deliberate guards on three hand-read rows, which is the same answer they got and is exactly the kind of agreement this exchange has already proven worthless twice. Two sessions finding the same thing is not confirmation when neither measured.

WHY I AM NOT MEASURING IT NOW, which is AC8 applied to myself rather than quoted at someone else. Running the classification today would produce a figure that sits in this note until the AC5 call is made, at which point it is a carried-forward number -- the precise defect of all five withdrawn claims in this exchange. The enumeration belongs AT the call, not before it. What belongs here is the query, so the call is cheap rather than open-ended:
  - population: every absence-shaped assertion in test/, pattern set stated and justified per AC3
  - classify each under AC12: does a positive establish THIS check's precondition over the same subject and the same source, and which precondition
  - then, separately, the question this note adds: of the rows that classify as paired, how many have a positive that exists for a reason OTHER than the test's own subject
The third bucket is the one that decides AC5, and neither repository has ever counted it. "82 of 83 are paired" and "0 of 83 are deliberately guarded" can both be true, and they point opposite ways: the first says the convention holds, the second says there is no convention at all, only scenarios that happen to require a positive over the same source. A mechanism cannot be judged against a convention nobody practices.

THE SHAPE ALL FIVE WITHDRAWALS SHARE, which is their formulation and I think the most portable thing produced here: not one of the five was a false statement when it was made. Each was true in the narrow reading it was written in and did work in a wider one -- "the paired form is house style 20 lines away", "82 of 83 are paired", "the author applied the rule and then dropped it", "the repair pattern exists twice", "that row is still safe". Each survived because the wider reading was the one being used and the narrow one was the one being defended. Recorded in this repository's CLAUDE.md profile in the same change, because a lesson about how to READ a claim has to be somewhere a session reads before it starts believing things, and a task note is not that place.

AC3 + AC8. THE QUERY, STATED WITH ITS SET AND ITS RULE, RE-MEASURED IN THIS FILE SET 2026-10-11 by this repository -- not carried from the filing.

PATTERN SET SEARCHED (grep -E over test/**/*.ts and test/**/*.tsx):
  .not.toContain( | .not.toMatch( | .not.toHaveProperty( | toHaveLength(0) | toEqual([]) | toBeUndefined( | toBeNull(
WHY THIS SET DEFINES ABSENCE-SHAPED ASSERTIONS: membership is decided by one property -- the assertion PASSES WHEN THE THING IT NAMES IS ABSENT -- not by the matcher family. Each member is satisfied by absence: a value missing from a collection (.not.toContain), a pattern missing from a string (.not.toMatch), a property missing from an object (.not.toHaveProperty), or the subject itself empty/absent (toHaveLength(0), toEqual([]), toBeUndefined, toBeNull).
EXCLUDED, WITH REASON: .not.toBe( (71 matches) and .not.toEqual( (4) are INEQUALITY -- a present value satisfies them, so they are not absence-shaped; .not.toThrow( (1) is about a call not throwing; .not.toBeUndefined( (3) is PRESENCE, the opposite.
